metadata.subject: DBMS
metadata.title: Explore Tables and Records
metadata.description: Use schemas, records, fields, and types to make safe table changes.

learning_objectives: Distinguish schema, columns, rows, and field values.
Use a schema to predict whether a record or edit is valid.
Explain why stable row identity matters.

mission.title: Work with a real table
mission.description: Predict each structural choice or change, then check the model consequence.

introduction.title: A table has structure and data
introduction.content: A schema names each column and its type. Every row is one record; each cell is a field value.
points: Columns describe the same kind of field across records.
Types prevent invalid values from entering a column.

worked_example.title: Read the structure before changing data
worked_example.content: Use the schema to interpret a student record.

steps.explanation: The schema defines the allowed columns and value types.
One complete row is a record with a stable row id.
A field is one value at a row-and-column intersection.

worked_example.conclusion: A valid change must preserve the schema while keeping row identity stable.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Predict each answer before revealing the model consequence.

action_explanations.identify-row: You identified a complete record by its stable row id.
action_explanations.identify-column: You identified the field shared down one column.
action_explanations.add-record: The schema decided whether the proposed record could be added.
action_explanations.edit-field: The column type decided whether the field edit was valid.

task.prompt: Which row id identifies Ben's complete record?
Which column stores every student's age?
Will this proposed record pass the schema, and how many rows will remain?
Will this edit pass the number type, and what age will remain?
Predict whether this mixed-type record is valid and the resulting row count.

challenge.title: Schema decision challenge
challenge.start_message: Use the schema, then predict the consequence.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep inspecting the table.

phases.title: Validate a record
phases.instruction: Decide whether the proposed record can be added and predict the row count.
phases.feedback: Recheck every proposed value against its column type.

guidance.start_message: Use the visible row and column labels.

items.content: A row id identifies one complete record.

phases.title: Read the table
phases.feedback: Use the row id, column name, and field intersection carefully.

guidance.start_message: Predict whether the schema accepts the change.

phases.title: Apply the schema
phases.instruction: Predict the validity and resulting row count.
phases.feedback: Check every required column and type.

guidance.start_message: Reason from the schema with no hints.

phases.title: Solve an edit
phases.instruction: Predict whether the edit occurs and the value that remains.
phases.feedback: Compare the proposed value with the field type.

guidance.start_message: Interpret an unfamiliar table task independently.

phases.title: Master the structure
phases.instruction: Solve the generated mixed-type table task.
phases.feedback: Separate schema rules from the current data.

thinking.title: Predict a hidden table consequence
thinking.instruction: Use the larger mixed-type schema. The resulting table is hidden until your prediction is checked.
thinking.do_not_execute: Inspect the schema, then predict validity and row count without applying the record.

prediction_fields.label: Schema validity
prediction_fields.prompt: Will the record be valid or invalid?

prediction_fields.label: Resulting row count
prediction_fields.prompt: How many records will the table contain?

feedback.all_correct: You reasoned correctly from the schema.

quiz.question: What decides whether a value is valid for a column?

discovery.title: Tables discovery
discovery.summary: Schemas describe structure; records contain data that must follow that structure.

sections.title: Schema
sections.content: The schema names columns and their types.

sections.title: Records
sections.content: Each row is one record with a stable identity.

sections.title: Fields
sections.content: A field is one value at a row-and-column intersection.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Changing data must not break the schema.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a form
alternate_explanations.content: A schema is like a form template; each completed form is one record.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through a row
alternate_explanations.content: student-2 identifies the row; age identifies the column; 21 is their intersecting field value.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how are schema and data different?
recall.model_answer: The schema defines allowed structure and types; rows contain the actual record values.
